Known quirks on this firmware:
- USB debugging opens port 5555 straight away; no Wireless debugging pairing needed.
- KEEP com.google.android.tv.remote.service. Besides the phone remote it carries the Bluetooth remote's
mic: with it disabled the mic button does nothing at all (no key event, no voice UI). Re-enabling it
brings the mic back. It holds the android.app.role.SYSTEM_TELEVISION_REMOTE_SERVICE role.
- The Wi-Fi network saved during first setup belongs to setupwraith (dumpsys wifi: OwnerUid = setupwraith's
uid). Forget and re-join it in Settings > Network & Internet before disabling setupwraith; afterwards it
shows cname=android.uid.system:1000. tools/disable.sh skips setupwraith until then.
- setupwraith's RecoveryActivity claims Home (priority 1) and goes before launcherx, as on the Chromecast.
- Voice search (Gemini / com.google.android.katniss) keeps working with launcherx disabled.
- Remote buttons (/vendor/usr/keylayout/Vendor_0957_Product_0031.kl):
YouTube = KEYCODE_BUTTON_3 and Free TV = KEYCODE_FEATURED_APP_1, both routed to launcherx, so they do
nothing once it is disabled. Netflix = KEYCODE_BUTTON_4; the Disney+ and Paramount+ buttons send
BUTTON_9 / BUTTON_10. Those three go to com.droidlogic's GlobalKeyReceiver ("oneTouchPlay"), which opens
the app, and for a disabled or missing app logs "Cannot find intent" or opens its Play Store page.
InputKeyService (INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 launcher/build-and-install.sh) with app_keys remaps them, checked
with the physical remote, e.g. in a theme's config.json:
"app_keys": ["KEYCODE_BUTTON_3:org.smarttube.stable", "KEYCODE_BUTTON_4:com.stremio.one",
"KEYCODE_FEATURED_APP_1:com.amarullz.androidtv.animetvjmto"]
- Free TV / "Freeplay" lives inside launcherx and goes with it.
- Google TV / Play Movies (com.google.android.videos) is not preinstalled on this box.
- Disabling dreamx leaves no screensaver set (screensaver_components was null; the default was dreamx).
Point it at the launcher's clock: settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream
- Animation scales already ship at 0.5x on this build.

onn update prompts (com.onn.updatenotification), remote firmware updates (com.google.android.tv.dfuservice),
com.gretzky.GlobalKey (onn remote app buttons), com.droidlogic.* (Amlogic vendor: HDMI, picture, remote
buttons), com.onn.bluetoothconnect (BT remote setup), com.google.android.tv.axel (remote audio routing),
Play Store / Play Services, Gboard.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- Unlike the Chromecast on Google TV 14, port 5555 is open as soon as USB debugging is on; no pairing.
- If a VPN app is connected, Settings > Network shows the VPN tunnel address, not the LAN one.
Find the box with `nc -z <lan>.x 5555` or `dns-sd -B _adb-tls-connect._tcp local.`.

QUIRKS ON THIS FIRMWARE:

1. Screensaver. screensaver_components ships as com.google.android.backdrop/.Backdrop with a
5-minute screen_off_timeout. Once backdrop is disabled the screensaver points at a disabled
component, so set another one:

(or com.android.dreams.basic/.Colors without the launcher).
2. Chromecast on a shared network. On this owner's Wi-Fi (a large shared network, ~150 hosts
across 192.168.1-18.x) about 150 devices held connections to the TV's Cast port 8009, and
YouTube kept pausing and then closing a few minutes into a video. The log showed the exit:
ActivityTaskManager: START u0 {act=MAIN cat=[HOME] ...} from uid 10043
uid 10043 is com.google.android.apps.mediashell. Disabling it fixed playback. Unlike the
50PUS8517 (its quirk 4), mediashell stayed disabled here 45 s after disabling; a reboot
check is still pending. Keep it (comment the line out) if you cast from your phone and your
network is your own.
3. lowmemorykiller is active even at idle with one app playing ("low watermark is breached and
thrashing"); this is a 1.38 GB low_ram set, so every background service removed helps.
4. Do not open com.mediatek.tv.factory or mediatek.factorymenu.ui to see what they do (see
PROMPT.md); they are left alone.
5. Boot to Live TV (EU unit). After a full reboot, Home comes up and about 0.2 s later system_server
sends android.mtk.intent.action.ACTION_REQUEST_TOP_RESUME to
com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter/.nav.TurnkeyUiMainActivity, so the TV lands in Live TV. Neither
settings list has a switch for it. A normal power-on from standby lands on Home.

Private DNS (dns.adguard-dns.com) works.
HDMI picture is still untested: nothing is plugged in. org.droidtv.eum and nettvregistration

Match on the BOARD and firmware, not on the model number. Philips/TP Vision ships one

board PH1M_EA_9970A should carry the same package set; a different board or a Google TV
(Android 12+) Philips will not. Check your own `pm list packages` against this file first —
`tools/tv.py --probe` prints model, Android version and build.

NOT the same platform as examples/philips-smart-4k-google-tv, which is a Skyworth-built
India-market set on Google TV 14 with com.smartdevice/com.sky/com.tianci packages and no
org.droidtv at all. Nothing from that file applies here and nothing here applies there.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/philips-50pus8517/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/philips-50pus8517/debloat.txt com.google.android.tvlauncher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (pass it to restore.sh, as above).
Live TV app:    org.droidtv.playtv
App labels below were resolved by pulling each APK and reading it with `aapt dump badging`,
not guessed from the package name. That matters on this firmware: org.droidtv.nettvapp4546 is
MEGOGO, nettvapp4655 is Deezer, nettvapp5512 is Fishing TV, and org.droidtv.candeebug is
labelled "DAC" and is the analytics uploader, not a debug tool.

QUIRKS ON THIS FIRMWARE, in the order they will bite you:

1. pm disable-user persists to /data/system/users/0/package-restrictions.xml with a delay
(~10 s on AOSP). If you run disable.sh and power-cycle the TV straight away, the changes
are silently lost: packages come back as enabled=0 (DEFAULT). Wait, or run
`pm list packages -d` and confirm your packages are listed before pulling the plug.
2. `adb reboot` over TCP hangs holding the dropped connection. Kill the adb server right
after sending it and wait on port 5555 coming back instead of on the adb command.
3. The Android 11 shell cannot disable individual components of another app
("SecurityException: Shell cannot change component state") and cannot `pm hide`
("Neither user 2000 nor current process has android.permission.MANAGE_USERS"). So if a
package refuses to stay disabled, the shell has no second lever. `pm suspend` does work
and survives a reboot, but it does not stop services: an app that starts itself from its
own boot receiver keeps running with suspended=true.
4. com.google.android.apps.mediashell (Chromecast built-in) could NOT be kept disabled on this
firmware and is deliberately absent from the list below. It returns to enabled=1 about 35 s
after every boot, reproducibly. pm disable-user, pm suspend, per-component disable and
pm hide were all tried; the first is undone, the second does not stop it, the last two are
refused by the platform. Left enabled, at a cost of about 37 MB.
5. A DISABLED PACKAGE CAN LEAVE A PERSISTENT PROCESS RETRYING FOREVER, AND pidof WILL NOT
SHOW IT. org.droidtv.xtv is the persistent TV engine and has five outbound service
bindings. Two of them, eum and aurora, were on the first version of this list, and
BOTH leave xtv in a permanent retry loop when disabled. Neither is in the list above now;
both are in the DO NOT DISABLE block below.

org.droidtv.eum -- bound via CONTEXTUALHELP. About five retries per second, logged as
xtvContextInterface ... connectCotextService - Service failed to connec i is null
51 of them in 10 seconds of an idle TV. This one also BREAKS A VISIBLE FUNCTION, and not
the one you would guess: the Philips sources drawer opens and vanishes within a second,
so HDMI inputs stop being reachable from the remote's SOURCES key. SourcesService logged
a correct, complete source list every time and the drawer still died.

org.droidtv.aurora -- about five retries per second too, logged as
xtvService: xtvService handleConnectAurora
at a steady 201 ms interval, 59 in 30 seconds of an idle TV. This one breaks nothing
visible and costs little: xtv sits at 0.2% of one core while doing it. It is log noise
plus a retry that can never succeed. Re-enabling it is free in practice -- aurora's
process does not start at idle even when the package is enabled, so xtv only needed the
package to be resolvable.

`pm enable` on either took its counter to zero immediately, with no reboot.

THE METHOD, which is the transferable part: a live PID proves the process exists, not
that it is healthy. xtv held the same PID through all eleven batches while both loops
ran. And do not grep for a string you already know -- that is how I missed the second
loop for a day after fixing the first. Clear the log, wait 30 seconds on an idle TV,
then group EVERYTHING by frequency and look at what repeats:
adb shell logcat -c; sleep 30; adb shell logcat -d > idle.txt
# then collapse digits and count: anything repeating several times a second is a loop
On this set that takes an idle log from 130 lines per 30 s down to 50, and the 50 that
remain are the firmware's own heartbeats.
6. The replacement launcher takes over on its own. Projectivy declares
android.intent.category.HOME, so the moment com.google.android.tvlauncher is disabled the
system resolves HOME to it — immediately, without a reboot and without enabling any
accessibility service. Check with
`cmd package resolve-activity --brief -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.HOME`
BEFORE disabling the stock launcher, and make sure your replacement is listed by
`cmd package query-activities` for that intent. If it is not, you will be left without a
home screen (see issue #90).

Android TV 11, firmware RTT2.211108.001 build 21029, security patch 2025-10-01, board PH1M_EA_9970A
ro.product.model=2021/22 Philips UHD Android TV  ro.product.device=PH1M_EA_9970A
Fingerprint: Philips/PH1M_EA_9970A/PH1M_EA_9970A:11/RTT2.211108.001/21029:user/release-keys
MediaTek MT5895, 2.67 GB RAM. Connected over Ethernet.

This is the same board AND the same firmware build as examples/philips-50pus8517, on an OLED
panel instead of an LED one. That file's quirks and its DO NOT DISABLE block apply here as
written; read them first. Nothing in its DO NOT DISABLE block is disabled below: eum, aurora,
xtv, playtv, contentexplorer, homeintentresolver and the browser engine all stay on.
This file lists what this unit disabled on top of, or instead of, that list.

Second unit: Philips 48OLED707/96 (48" OLED with Ambilight), Taiwan, on Wi-Fi.
Same board, same RTT2.211108.001 firmware, but an older build: 2769, security patch 2023-08-05.
Fingerprint: Philips/PH1M_EA_9970A/PH1M_EA_9970A:11/RTT2.211108.001/2769:user/release-keys
ro.boot.device_name and the global device_name read 48OLED707/96; 2.67 GB RAM as above.
- Out of the box, org.droidtv.freeviewplayers and 15 uk.co.freeview.* apps were already disabled,
so they are not something to add here.
- Wi-Fi: com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith was KEPT on this unit, as this list advises.
com.google.android.tvrecommendations was kept too, so the notification panel stays.
- Everything else in this file that is installed on the set was disabled, and on top of it these
entries from examples/philips-50pus8517: partnersetup, onetimeinitializer, sss.authbridge,
syncadapters.calendar, nettvapp4655 (Deezer), m7opapp, marvin.talkback, Prime Video
(com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom), dlna and ipcontrol. CHILI, Singa, Pluto TV, Rakuten TV and
nettvapp4546/4932/5527 are not installed on this unit.
- All of them were still disabled after a restart, and the replacement launcher stayed Home.
Idle-loop check after the debloat (50PUS8517 quirk 5 method, 30 s): 186 lines, no line repeating
more than 10 times; the top repeater was WifiVendorHal's link-layer stats poll.
- Screensaver on an OLED: the firmware does not let Android's screensaver start on a timer. At every
boot org.droidtv.tv.tptvservice (TPTvServiceReceiver) puts screen_off_timeout and sleep_timeout back
to 604800000 ms, "Never", logging "screensaver put when to start is not never". A shorter "When to
start", from the TV's settings or `settings put system screen_off_timeout`, works until the next
boot and is then reset. Read from the receiver's code; the same strings are in the Android 9 build
of tptvservice on PH9M_EA_5599 (examples/philips-tpm191e). What survives a reboot is the launcher's
own idle clock: "home_idle_clock_minutes": 3 in a theme. It drifts the clock to spare the panel and
starts only on Home, never over an app or Live TV. Checked here: the clock came up after 3 minutes
on Home.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/philips-55oled707/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/philips-55oled707/debloat.txt com.google.android.tvlauncher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher
Live TV app:    org.droidtv.playtv
App labels were read from each APK with `aapt dump badging`, not guessed from package names.

What this unit adds to the 50PUS8517 notes:

1. org.droidtv.nettvbrowser is needed on a UK set. With it disabled, ITVX (a Freeview Play
app) hung while BBC iPlayer still worked. It is re-enabled here, as the browser-engine
entry in the 50PUS8517 DO NOT DISABLE block says it should be.
2. com.phorus.playfi.tv (Play-Fi) could NOT be kept disabled and is commented out below, like
mediashell in 50PUS8517 quirk 4. It came back after both full restarts, with enabled=1
(ENABLED), not 0 (DEFAULT): something re-enables it on purpose, so this is not the ~10 s
persistence delay (50PUS8517 quirk 1). Every other package stayed disabled. The likely
source is org.droidtv.tv.tptvservice, which must stay and which posts a notification on a
PlayFi_ChannelID channel at every boot. That link is not proven.
3. org.droidtv.homeintentresolver ships with its HomeActivity component already disabled
(`pm dump` lists it under disabledComponents), so it does not compete for Home. While
com.google.android.tvlauncher is enabled it wins Home at priority 2 and
`cmd package set-home-activity` does not stick; once it is disabled, the replacement
launcher takes Home immediately (50PUS8517 quirk 6).
4. uk.co.freeview.mdsclient (Freeview Play metadata) crash-loops in the background, several
times in a few minutes. It did this before anything was disabled, so it is the firmware,
not this list. Each crash logs DeadSystemException, which looks alarming and is not.
5. Idle-loop check (50PUS8517 quirk 5 method, 30 s, TV in standby): 163 lines, no line
repeating more than 15 times, and nothing tied to a disabled package. The top repeaters
were cast_shell (a phone probing Chromecast) and the tuner's signal-level poll.

Verified after a full restart (off at the wall): the replacement launcher stays Home, ITVX
plays, channel changes and the TV guide work with Alexa disabled, the SOURCES drawer stays
open and lists HDMI 1-4, and the red button opens HbbTV.

Memory, read from `dumpsys meminfo` at idle on the home screen. The two readings straddle a
restart, so treat the difference as approximate:
Stock:                     1,624 MB used PSS,   712 MB free, 326 MB in swap
This list + a new launcher: 1,389 MB used PSS,  831 MB free,  80 MB in swap
In a 30-minute Netflix session afterwards, free memory stayed between 814 and 939 MB with no
low-memory kills.

Kept on purpose: Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell), Ambilight and Hue, the
Philips browser, DLNA, IP control, firmware updates, and every streaming app this household
uses (Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, YouTube, Apple TV, the Freeview Play apps).

PH1M_EA_9970A, com.google.android.tvlauncher) nor philips-75pus8505 (Android TV 12, PH9M). This is the

ATSC and ISDB tuners, com.omni.ssutv.*, and the regional org.droidtv.*config packages.

Applied in small batches on 2026-10-21 with a screenshot and a 30 s idle-log check (50PUS8517 quirk 5
method) after each. No retry loop appeared; the idle log went from 865 to ~690 lines per 30 s.
Home, inputs (HDMI 2 with a PS5), Live TV, Settings, YouTube playback and every remote button were
checked the same day; not yet lived with for days. If something breaks, `pm enable <package>` and report it.
After a reboot `pm list packages -d` was identical: nothing re-enabled itself on this firmware, Play-Fi
and Chromecast included (unlike the 55OLED707 and 50PUS8517). Checked again 8.5 min after boot.

Memory, `dumpsys meminfo` on the home screen; readings straddle a reboot, so approximate:
Stock:                      1,755 MB used PSS (launcherx 182 MB across two processes)
This list + launcher/:      1,582 MB used PSS (com.gathin.tvhome 159 MB)

Quirks on this firmware:
1. org.droidtv.demome asks for TV_INPUT_HARDWARE here, so tools/disable.sh refuses it (#321). Kept.
2. Remote buttons go through org.droidtv.GlobalKey, which hard-codes two of them to the stock launcher:
the gear button (scancode 141, KEY_SETUP) starts launcherx/.dashboard.DashboardActivity and the
Apps button (scancode 779, keycode 813) sends ALL_APPS. With launcherx disabled both do nothing.
Fixed with the launcher's HomeKeyService (HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1): settings_key_scancodes 141 and
app_keys 813:com.gathin.tvhome. Matching the gear button by keycode (327) did NOT work, by
scancode it does; checked with the real remote. SOURCES (768), Netflix (772), YouTube (776), TV
(170, last source) and Quick menu (765) are handled by GlobalKey itself and keep working.
TV Guide (172) does nothing on a set with no channels tuned, before and after.
3. The org.droidtv.candeebug CollectionService is bound by 22 TV processes; none retried after it was
disabled. tv.samba.ssm is bound by org.droidtv.tv.tptvservice:SambaService, also no retries.
4. Settings references io.mimi.tvapp and tpvaudiomanager sends Mimi a broadcast; with both Mimi
packages disabled the sound menus still open.

Kept on purpose: AirPlay (com.mediatek.partner.airplay_sys, AirplayAPK, airplaydaemon), Google

IP control, Ambilight, BrowseHere and the Vewd browser, and the streaming apps this household uses
(Netflix, YouTube, YouTube Music, Prime Video, HBO Max, Apple TV).

What this unit adds to the 50PUS8517 / 55OLED707 notes:

1. Already disabled at the factory on this French unit: the UK Freeview apps (uk.co.freeview.*,
org.droidtv.freeviewplayers), Apple TV, YouTube Music AND org.droidtv.aurora. The 50PUS8517 notes say a
disabled aurora leaves xtv retrying every 201 ms; on this unit an idle 30 s log shows 0 handleConnectAurora
and 0 connectCotextService lines, so aurora was left as the factory set it.
2. Packages the earlier lists do not have, checked with `dumpsys package` (none launched):
org.droidtv.astrahdplus (HD+ German satellite info pages), io.mimi.tvapp + io.mimi.sdk.service (Mimi
hearing-personalised sound), org.droidtv.dropboxprovider (Dropbox in Media). All three disabled cleanly;
sound, Media and live TV unaffected. Not touched: org.droidtv.fastip (IP channel installer; the 75PUS8505
notes say SOURCES dies without it), org.droidtv.sam / csm (service menus), dukservice, usbbreakin, factory.
3. tools/tv.py (adb_shell) gets no answer until it is accepted at the TV's own "Allow USB debugging?" prompt,
even with the same key the stock adb already uses; tools/theme.sh hangs on it until then. The stock adb works.
4. OLED screensaver: tvsystemui draws a moving Philips logo over everything after about 5 minutes of a still
picture, and once it is up it stays on top of the launcher's own idle clock. home_idle_clock_minutes must
therefore be 4 or less here; with the clock already up (it moves every minute) the logo did not come back
in more than 7 minutes. Injected keys over adb do not dismiss the logo, and the shell cannot write to the
remote's input device on this firmware (sendevent: Permission denied), so test it with the real remote.
5. The TV powers on to the last source in use: switched off from Home it comes back on Home, switched off on
an HDMI input it comes back on that input. Nothing to fix.
6. Chromecast (mediashell) re-enables itself, as on the 50PUS8517: left out.

about 780 MB stock, about 1.1 GB with this list and the launcher.

Launcher handover, two things that differ from the script's assumptions on this TV:
1. The first cold start of the freshly installed, not yet compiled launcher takes longer than the
10 s `am start -W` waits on this 32-bit MT5887, so build-and-install.sh stops with
"Status: timeout" although the launcher came up fine (it was the resumed activity and drew its
first screen). The remaining steps (pm grant, cmd package compile -m speed, set-home-activity)
were run by hand. Updating the already installed launcher later started in 2.2 s and the
script ran through on its own.
2. The stock launcher's HOME filter has priority=2, a third-party launcher's always 0, and Android
picks the higher priority before it looks at the preferred activity. So with the stock launcher
still enabled, set-home-activity succeeds and the HOME role moves to com.gathin.tvhome, yet the
Home key still opens com.google.android.tvlauncher. The new launcher only takes over once the
stock one is disabled, as note 3 in examples/philips-55oled707 found on the Android 11 board.

After each batch: logcat -c, 30 s of an idle TV, logcat -d, then group lines by shape and look
for anything repeating several times a second (see quirk 5 in examples/philips-50pus8517). The
only loop on this TV before and after is adbd retrying the USB gadget about once a second while
USB debugging is on; it is not caused by the debloat.
A soundbar on HDMI ARC that goes to standby on its own silence timer sends <Set System Audio Mode>
off and <Terminate ARC>, and the TV shows "TV reproduktory aktivní" (TV speakers active). With
Home on screen and nothing playing that happens during testing too; it is the soundbar, not the
debloat.

Leave com.homwee.factory (factory menu, see the CHiQ notes), com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard (the Live TV
channel-scan wizard) and com.homwee.synckey enabled. The last one is a privileged system app (android.uid.system)
that starts at boot and talks to the factory. The physical remote and HDMI path
go through com.mediatek.tv.service and com.mediatek.tvinput, not through this list.

KEEP com.google.android.leanbacklauncher.partnercustomizer: provides the tvlauncher.widget
content provider. Disabling it causes com.mediatek.tv.service to crash-loop after the next
reboot ("Failed to find provider tvlauncher.widget") and remote hotkeys stop working.

Tested on both sets: Home opens, Netflix / Flow / Max / YouTube still
resolve, Chromecast (mediashell) comes back after re-enable, HDMI stays in Inputs.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- USB debugging alone opens network ADB on port 5555. On realme firmware UKNV.260514.001,
Developer options also offers Wireless debugging with pairing.
- After a reboot the TV may take a new DHCP address.
- com.cltv.fast is automatically re-enabled by the Changhong vendor firmware at every boot.
- com.homwee.chtvmanager ("TV Manager") can be safely disabled with pm disable-user --user 0
without uninstallation.
- The default IME is already Gboard. No Baidu-keyboard quirk.
- Disabling com.google.android.tvrecommendations does not clear the stock
launcher's poster rows. Those go away only after launcher/ replaces Home.
Disable com.google.android.tvlauncher only once the new home is the default,
or Home can land on a factory activity.

AIWA AW32B4SMG variant (two sets, tested the same day, three batches with screenshots, one reboot each):
- Differences in the list: keep com.homwee.upgrade and com.homwee.dmt.upgrade (comment them out) to keep
firmware updates. com.homwee.alexacontrol is not installed. com.homwee.chtvmanager was disabled instead of
uninstalled. Chromecast (mediashell), voice (katniss), com.homwee.multiscreenshare ("Midiacast"),
com.homwee.mmp.screenshare, Netflix, YouTube Music and Play Games were also disabled, by the owner's choice.
- setupwraith was left enabled on both AIWA sets (comment it out to match) and the new launcher still owns
Home. The saved Wi-Fi belonged to com.google.uid.shared on one set and android.uid.system on the other.

Notes from this firmware:
- ADB: Settings -> About -> press OK on 产品型号 (product model) 7 times to unlock developer mode,
then Settings -> 账号与安全 (Account & Security) -> ADB 调试 -> 允许. Network ADB (port 5555) closes
on every reboot; turn it on again there after each power cycle. Standby is not a reboot.
- `pm disable-user --user 0` is accepted for the shell user (unlike MiTV-ANTL0, which needs `pm hide`).
- Home: the framework filters third-party HOME candidates by a package-name allowlist, the same
mechanism as MiTV-AETP0 (services.vdex has isThirdpartyHomeAllowed and
APP_WHITELIST_ALLOW_THIRDPARTY_HOME; the list is /data/system/mitv_security_center.xml, not readable
from the shell). The standard com.gathin.tvhome build installed and opened, and
`cmd package set-home-activity` printed Success, but HOME still resolved to com.mitv.tvhome.
The opt-in application-ID build from docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-aetp0-dofus.md
(`./gradlew assembleRelease -PlauncherApplicationId=com.ts.launcher`) became Home with
com.mitv.tvhome still enabled, and stayed Home after a full reboot. Do not run
launcher/build-and-install.sh with its defaults here: it would disable com.mitv.tvhome, and
disabling the stock launcher leaves no allowed Home. Use the manual commands in that doc.
- Settings: android.settings.SETTINGS and android.settings.WIFI_SETTINGS resolve to nothing; the
launcher's Settings pill falls back to com.xiaomi.mitv.settings/.entry.MainActivity, which opened.
- App grid: the streaming apps declare LEANBACK_LAUNCHER and show up; Xiaomi settings, weather and
TV Manager are LAUNCHER-only. com.mitv.alarmcenter declares LEANBACK_LAUNCHER (hide it with
hidden_apps if you don't want a 定时提醒 tile).
- Inputs: com.mediatek.tvinput registers HDMI HW5-HW8, AV HW2, component HW3, VGA HW4 and tuners
HW0/HW1. Nothing was plugged in, so switching from the launcher's Inputs menu was not tested.
- Startup ad: `settings put system boot_ad_switch 0` (it was null before) removed it, checked after
a full reboot with stock launcher 3.49.1601. boot_ad, boot_ad_sound_enable and boot_ad_switch_show
were already 0 and did not stop the ad. Undo: `settings delete system boot_ad_switch`.
See docs/devices/xiaomi-l43m7-ea-antl0.md for the same key on an older launcher.
- Screenshots: `screencap` exits 1 with a 0-byte file while PatchWall's home is on screen (it shows a
sideband video layer); it works over the replacement launcher, settings and the screensaver.
- com.gitvdemo.video is 银河奇异果 (GITV's licensed iQIYI app, label checked with aapt), a streaming
app, not a promo reel. Kept here.
- com.mitv.care ("adcare") is disabled by the factory already.

Deliberately NOT disabled:
- mitv.service, com.xiaomi.mitv.tvplayer, com.mediatek.* (inputs, tuner), com.xiaomi.mitv.settings,
com.xiaomi.mitv.systemui, com.sohu.inputmethod.sogou.tv (the only keyboard), com.android.bluetooth,

- mediatek.factorymenu.ui and com.mstar.android.media.tests are factory tools: never start them.
- com.mitv.screensaver: the stock flip-clock screensaver stays until another one is selected.
- com.xiaomi.mitv.tvpush.tvpushservice: besides push it carries
com.xiaomi.mitv.getwhitelist.GetInstallerWhiteList, and this firmware has an install blacklist
(pi_config in Settings.System). Not disabled, so app installs were not put at risk.
- com.xiaomi.mitv.smartpanel: MiTV-ANSP0 disabled it, MiTV-MFFU0 says it is the Menu-button panel. Kept.
- Kept by this owner's choice: voice remote (com.xiaomi.voicecontrol, com.xiaomi.wakeupservice,
com.xiaomi.mitv.tvmanager, com.mitv.alarmcenter), casting (com.xiaomi.miplay,
com.xiaomi.mitv.smartshare, com.duokan.airkan.tvbox, com.xiaomi.wfdsinkhelperservice,
com.xiaomi.mi_connect_service), firmware updates (com.xiaomi.mitv.upgrade, ~47 MB resident),
payments (com.xiaomi.mitv.pay, com.xiaomi.mitv.payment), karaoke (com.xiaomi.mitv.karaoke.service),

mau.header:
Skyworth 65A3F (7T641_A3F, MediaTek MT9633), China, Android 13 (API 33), build 10.01.250328
Chinese Coocaa/CCOS firmware, no GMS. Stock home is com.coocaa.aigc.home
(com.coocaa.aigc.home.home.rootpage.HomeActivity): it is launched at boot and it also takes the
remote's HOME key, although the only HOME-category activity is the third-party launcher.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/skyworth-65a3f/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/skyworth-65a3f/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

com.coocaa.aigc.home must stay ENABLED. Tried on the TV 2026-10-21:
- `pm disable-user` restarts the framework and the package comes back enabled by itself.
- `pm suspend` brings up com.coocaa.os.control/.ui.QrActivity, a WeChat QR unlock screen.
- `pm hide`, component-level disables and `su` are all refused; with no root /system/xbin/su
fails with "setgid failed: Operation not permitted".
- Disabling it and rebooting leaves the TV with no home: it hangs on the SKYWORTH logo, the
network stack never starts and 5555 disappears. Recovery was a factory reset from Recovery
(power off, hold the hidden touch button under the logo while plugging the set back in,
wipe data/factory reset).

Ads on this firmware: com.tianci.ad BootService draws the boot ad, its PowerOffActivity the
shutdown ad, and the same package hosts the ad landing pages. Disabling it removed both;
checked across a reboot with zero logcat hits for the package.

Quirks, all checked on the TV:
- 5555 opens without pairing (ro.adb.secure=0), so any host on the LAN gets a shell.
- adbd's stdout wrapper corrupts `exec-out screencap -p` here as well; screencap to a file on
the TV and pull it.
- `tools/tv.py --push` is for small files. b64push.py needed roughly 20 minutes for a 17 MB
APK. Faster: hold an adb shell running `toybox nc -l -p 9999 > /data/local/tmp/x.apk` and
send from the computer with `nc <tv ip> 9999 < x.apk` (about 100 s; verify with md5sum, the
adb_shell read timeout can fire at 120 s even when the file arrived intact).

A third-party launcher cannot own the boot screen:
- boot_start_tv_source only picks the input source (DEFAULT/REMEMBER, HOME, CHANNEL); there is
no "launch an app" value, and HOME changes nothing.
- Two one-press routes work. (1) The remote's colour key:
com.skyworth.setting/.module.device.shortcutkey.ShortcutKeySetActivity lists the installed
launcher and the binding sticks — press the colour key, the launcher opens. (2) The stock
home's dock: com.coocaa.aigc.home/.dockedit.DockEditActivity, after a reboot the launcher sits
in the left rail. `cmd package set-home-activity` also succeeds and the launcher does become
the default HOME, but the boot screen and the HOME key still go to aigc.home.

Kept on purpose: com.coocaa.aigc.home, com.skyworth.setting, com.tianci.system, com.coocaa.os.*
(including com.coocaa.os.control and com.coocaa.os.softsettings), com.coocaa.safelauncher,
com.tianci.movieplatform, input methods, voice/mic, casting and audio/PQ packages.
com.overseas.store.appstore is absent after a factory reset; the line is harmless there.

CRITICAL SAFETY TRAPS (READ BEFORE USING). Full details: docs/devices/skyworth-8r40-k5c.md
1. The ONLY ADB toggle lives inside Settings > 基本设置 > 设备信息 (About this TV) > 更多信息.
That page crashes if any of these are disabled:
com.tianci.de
com.skyworthdigital.stb.dataprovider
com.coocaa.sky.ccapi
A crashed About page means ADB can never be re-enabled: factory reset is the only way out.
BEFORE debloating, install Activity Launcher (de.szalkowski.activitylauncher.oss) and confirm you
can open com.tianci.setting/.factorysetting.FactorySetting (action coocaa.intent.action.TIANCI_FACTORY).
Apply in small batches and re-open the About page after each batch.
2. DO NOT DISABLE com.tianci.movieplatform (stock launcher) or any other current launcher.
HOME is hardcoded in read-only /system/pcfg and no package declares category HOME, so disabling
the launcher gives a black screen on boot (sys.boot_completed never set).
3. Do not touch persist.service.homepage.* props. Setting persist.service.homepage.switch 0 stopped
adbd from starting after reboot on the reporter's unit.

Boot ad (not a package, run once over ADB, survives reboot):
tools/tv.py 'setprop persist.sys.bootvideo.time 1'

- Port 5555 goes flaky: opens when USB debugging is switched, may close again on its own, and
the adb client can go "offline" mid-session; reconnect with `adb connect <ip>:5555`.
The stock adb client (platform-tools 37.0.1) authenticates reliably; delete tools/adbkey to let
tools/tv.py fall back to ~/.android/adbkey when the TV already trusts that key.

answers before ADB does).
- `adb exec-out screencap -p` is corrupted by an adbd stdout wrapper ("Init wrapper sys mutex
successful", LF->CRLF). Screenshots must go screencap to a file + `adb pull`.
- No dedicated updater package; com.smartdevice.aftersale can push APKs on boot, so it is disabled.

every one disabled cleanly, but two things differ:

intent filter at priority=2, which outranks the preference `cmd package set-home-activity` writes:
it prints Success while `resolve-activity` keeps naming launcherx. Disabling setupwraith alone did
not hand Home over either, so the note above about leaving launcherx enabled does not hold here.

booted to the new launcher since. Check with `dumpsys activity activities | grep mFocusedApp`, not

factory; sonyselect and seeds.iot.remotestart are enabled too and were not named either way above.

and recovery.py records that, so undo leaves them alone.

Second VU31, same build, 2026-10-20: the extra lines marked (2nd) disabled in batches with a screenshot and
crash-log check after each, then the launcher installed and Home switched, reboot-checked. Notes from it:
- Live TV and every HDMI/AV input play in com.android.tv; the inputs come from com.realtek.tv.passthrough
(HDMI 1-3, a CEC soundbar on HDMI 3, Video). In the launcher set live_tv_package to com.android.tv and
hide it. The Input key opens smartui's menu system-wide, so no INPUT_KEY_SERVICE is needed.
- Before disabling setupwraith check `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`: here the network belonged to
android.uid.system, so Wi-Fi and ADB stayed up.
- com.sony.dtv.applicationdisabler re-enables com.sony.dtv.ecodashboard at every boot (as on the BF1), so
it is not listed; hide its tile in the launcher (hidden_apps) instead.
- Sony's Timers & Clock declares two leanback activities with one label, which showed as two tiles
(launcher fix in #298).
- Real remote checked after the switch: Home, Input, the mic and the app buttons all work.

Third VU31, same build, 2026-10-21: the list above plus the launcher, reboot-checked. On this set the remote's
app buttons did NOT work once launcherx was off:
- Realtek's com.realtek.advancesetting owns the app buttons (`dumpsys window policy`: KEYCODE_BUTTON_2/4/14/15
go to its GlobalKeyReceiver), but on Google TV it does not open the app itself: Utils.startApp hands every
launch to launcherx's globalbutton.GlobalButtonLaunch_Receiver whenever the
com.google.android.feature.AMATI_EXPERIENCE feature is present. With launcherx disabled that broadcast has no
receiver and the press does nothing; logcat shows "Failed to find provider info for
...launcherx.coreservices.DeviceModeContentProvider".
- Fix for four of them: app_keys in the launcher with INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1, which catches the keycode first:
201:com.google.android.youtube.tv, 202:com.google.android.youtube.tv (second YouTube button),
191:com.netflix.ninja, 189:com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom. Checked with the real remote.
- SonyLIV (3004) and JioHotstar (3006) cannot be fixed this way: Realtek's KeyEventManager delivers those Sony
codes to advancesetting only, they never reach Android's input pipeline, so no accessibility service sees
them. Only re-enabling launcherx brings those two buttons back.
- InputKeyService also takes the Input key, but com.android.tv.action.VIEW_INPUTS resolves to
com.sony.dtv.smartui/.select.SmartSelectActivity here, the same menu the button opened before.
- The Ambient screensaver (dreamx) keeps working with launcherx disabled, for owners who want to keep it.
- com.android.camera2 is installed and crashes on open (the set has no camera); disabled here, not listed
because it has not been lived with yet.

Notes from this firmware:
- Android 9 has no topResumedActivity line: check apps and inputs with
`dumpsys activity activities | grep mResumedActivity`, and the input with
`dumpsys tv_input | sed -n '/sessionStateMap/,$p' | grep inputId` (HDMI 1 = ExternalTvInputService/HW2).

false positive here; no TVINPUT_ALLOW needed while it stays off.
- Launcher works: built from launcher/ and installed with build-and-install.sh, which disables tvlauncher
(HOME priority 2) before set-home-activity. Home confirmed with `dumpsys window | grep mFocusedApp`
(on Android 9 it is in dumpsys window, not dumpsys activity) before and after a reboot; Netflix,
YouTube, Input, Settings and Home on the real remote all work without the accessibility services.

First VH2 list on Android 10 (the other BRAVIA_VH2 / VH21 lists are Android 12) and the first
China-market VH2 build, so the package set differs from all of them: this firmware has no
tv.samba.ssm, no com.sony.dtv.promos / sonyselect / sonytab, no com.google.android.feedback and no
Play Store, so there is no Sony ACR or recommendation row to remove here. The ad surfaces on a
China set are the Dangbei home and store and the preinstalled content apps.

Stock Home on this firmware is com.dangbei.TVHomeLauncher (ChinaHome). It is left enabled as the
fallback, which is why restore.sh is given it rather than com.google.android.tvlauncher. Pass the
owner's own launcher instead if that is what owns HOME on your unit. Live TV / player:
com.sony.dtv.tvx.
Keep the com.sony.dtv.tvinput.* services, tvapi, sonysystemservice, sonyvendorservice,
settingsprovider, systemupdate/update, partnerkeycn (DRM), braviasync*, imeproxy, webapi.core,
irbservice, devicecontrolservice, homenetwork, searchapp, notificationcenter, HappyCast
(com.hpplay.happyplay.aw, the only casting path on a set without Google Cast), the Dangbei store
(com.sony.dangbeimarket) and every com.mediatek.* package: they drive HDMI, the tuner, DRM, CEC,
the remote, OTA and casting. None of them is in this list.

Checked on the TV over wired Ethernet with network ADB on 5555:
- 47 packages are disabled on this set in total. The 13 that were already disabled at the factory
or by an earlier session (setupwraith, mysony, iot, livingfit, smarthelp, eulaviewer, braviashow,
smartmediaapp, b2b.softap, b2b.vendorprotocol, screnmirroring.com, dreams.basic,
providers.contacts) are not in this list, so restore.sh leaves them as they were.
- All 34 below survived `adb reboot` (pm list packages -d still showed them) and none had a process
again afterwards, including the PERSISTENT com.sony.dtv.b2b.hotelmode: unlike the X9000H Android
12 report, system_server did not start it again on this build.
- MemAvailable went from 1,053,752 kB to 1,092,224 kB without a reboot, and SwapFree from 49,404 kB
(53 MB already swapped out) to 102,396 kB after the reboot. The processes below measured about
103 MB of PSS together while they were still running. Most of the RAM on this set belongs to user
apps, not to anything in this list, so expect a smaller win than on a 1.5 GB set.
- After the reboot HOME still resolved to the owner's launcher, the Home key returned to it, HDMI
1-4 still enumerated, tvinput / sonysystemservice / tvx / webapi.core / systemupdate were still
running, `logcat -b crash` had no new FATAL entry and a screenshot was a normal 1920x1080 frame.
- `svc power reboot` is refused on this firmware (PowerManagerService.reboot, SecurityException);
`adb reboot` works.
- Applied and reboot-checked on 22 October 2026, not yet lived with for days. If something breaks,
re-enable it with `pm enable <package>` and please report it.

TESTING, honestly: applied in three rounds on 2026-10-20 and used for a few hours only, which is
shorter than CONTRIBUTING.md asks. What was actually checked, each after a reboot: Netflix and
YouTube open and play, HDMI input switching works, the Live TV source picker works, Wi-Fi survives,
picture/sound settings open, the firmware update check still runs, the screensaver still starts.
The full list was also restored (tools/restore.sh) and re-applied once, so the undo path is tested
on this unit. I will report back if something breaks.

Measured effect on this unit, idle, settled, after reboot:
MemAvailable 307 MB -> 363 MB with the stock launcher (+56 MB), 391 MB with launcher/ (+84 MB).
This TV is RAM-bound, not I/O-bound: 0% iowait, ~88% idle CPU, but ~330 MB of zram swap in use.
Every MB freed here is a MB less swapped, which is why debloating helps this set noticeably.

Unit-specific notes (these differ from the 40S5400A list, check yours before copying):
- The saved Wi-Fi network belongs to com.android.tv.settings, NOT setupwraith, so setupwraith is
safe to disable here and the network survives. disable.sh checks this for you; do not force it.
- The photo screensaver (com.google.android.backdrop) must be swapped before it is disabled:
tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.android.dreams.basic/.Colors'
(restore: com.google.android.backdrop/com.google.android.backdrop.Backdrop)
- com.tcl.usercenter does NOT stay disabled. com.tcl.ttvs contains a service logging as
"OverSeasAppShow" which reads /tclconfig/software/param/apps/app_EU_4K.json and re-enables it,
at every boot and again whenever ttvs itself restarts. Disabling com.tcl.ttvs does not help:
it is re-enabled too. /tclconfig is mounted ro and is not even readable from an adb shell.
The entry is left in the list because it does get disabled; it just does not stay that way.
- On this set "standby" from the remote is a full power-down: the TV leaves the network entirely
and cold-boots on the next power-on. There is no network wake, and nothing applied with adb that
the firmware re-asserts at boot will survive being switched off.

PRE-EXISTING FIRMWARE BUG, not caused by debloating (verified by restoring every package to stock,
rebooting, and reproducing it again):
com.android.tv.settings crashes every single time you leave the Settings app.
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Service not registered:
com.tcl.android.tv.settings.accounts.TCLAccountManager$1
at TCLAccountManager.destroyManager -> MainSettings.onDestroy
In TvSettings 1.3.0, destroyManager() calls unbindService() on the Activity context while
bindRemoteServiceIfNeverBind() binds on the Application context, and it guards on mInstall
("is the TCL User Center activity installed") instead of isConnection, so it also double-unbinds.
The correctly written sibling method unbindRemoteServiceIfHasBind() is right there in the class.
Workaround while the TV stays on: disabling com.tcl.usercenter makes mInstall false and the bad
branch is skipped (verified, 0 crashes over repeated open/exit cycles). It does not survive a
power cycle, see the note above. Mentioned here so nobody files it against this project.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- The stock launcher declares HOME priority 2, so `cmd package set-home-activity` alone does not

idle, so it is left in the list.
- com.tcl.ttvs is NOT text-to-speech: its activities are versionUpdateApp SystemUpdateActivity and
NetworkUpdateActivity, i.e. the firmware updater. Keep it for OTA updates.
- After a reboot the system can switch to the last HDMI source on its own (com.tcl.tv started by
uid 1000 about 2 s after Home). Seen once; a PS5 on HDMI-CEC may be the trigger. Home brings
the launcher back.

disabling it, switch to the AOSP one:

Known quirks on this firmware:
- The remote's gear button sends keycode 83 (KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION, scancode 561), which only launcherx
handled: set settings_key_keycodes to [83] (config.xml or a theme) so it opens Settings again.
- On both models, launcherx is disabled only after CleanYourTV owns Home; build-and-install does it,
and restore.sh needs launcherx as its argument.
- HomeKeyService, used for the gear button, can stop volume long-press from repeating on some TCL
Google TV builds: holding volume then steps once. Set key_filter=false to restore the repeat and
lose the remapped keys, or leave HomeKeyService off. Not measured on the 32V5C; see
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md.
- With katniss off the mic button does nothing; leave it enabled if you use voice.
- Usage statistics restart empty after a power cut (they are written to disk only now and then).

Stock launcher is com.google.android.tvlauncher and it has HOME priority 2 on this firmware: it
must be disabled, or set-home-activity reports Success and HOME still lands on it. Install the
replacement launcher first, otherwise disable.sh will skip that line for its own HOME guard.

Factory menu from the remote, no software needed:
Settings > Picture > Advanced Settings > Brightness, highlight Contrast, type 1 9 5 0
then Other > ADB. Developer options > USB debugging must be on as well, or the RSA dialog never
appears and adb says "unauthorized". service.adb.tcp.port is preset to 5555 by the vendor, so
ADB comes up on the network, not USB.

WARNING - 1-Factory menu > NVM reset wipes the Wi-Fi MAC, the Widevine keybox and the Netflix
ESN. It is not a one-step operation: after the NVM reset do a factory data reset AND reflash the
full firmware over USB. Only the reflash re-provisions the vendor data; stopping earlier leaves a
02:00:00:00:00:00 Wi-Fi MAC and Netflix error -121 for good.

Inputs menu, Settings, Chromecast and the Bluetooth remote all kept working. MemAvailable went from 557 MB to

- Settings > Applications opens TCL "TV Guard" (com.tcl.tvweishi), and still does while it is disabled.

Same G10 platform and build as tcl-g10-google-tv/, but with Middle East preloads (OSN+, Disney+ MEA,
iQIYI, Shahid) and nothing disabled at the factory: logkit, Samba TV ACR and ttvs all ship ENABLED.

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-55p7k/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
Lived with for a day and a reboot so far, with a custom launcher as Home; nothing broke.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV / HDMI app: com.tcl.tv.
Keep: com.tcl.tv, com.tcl.tvinput, com.tcl.suspension (the Input picker, VIEW_INPUTS), com.tcl.dashboard,
com.tcl.autopair, com.tcl.systemserver, com.android.tv.settings (also runs TCL's quick panels).
com.tcl.browser is kept here because the remote's Web key opens it.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- Same as the other G10 sets: setupwraith claims Home once launcherx is disabled, so it goes too.
- The remote sends Settings as KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION (83), Netflix and YouTube as KEYCODE_TCL_NETFLIX and
KEYCODE_TCL_YOUTUBE, and the Web key as raw code 4159. Keys injected with `input keyevent` never reach
an accessibility service; test remaps with the real remote.
- Android's screen_brightness does nothing (TCL drives the backlight). TCL's own Audio Only mode turns
the panel off with sound playing: `am startservice -a com.tcl.settings.SHOW_WINDOW -p
com.android.tv.settings --es Type AudioOnly`.
- App log lines rarely show up in logcat (64K buffer); write diagnostics to a file instead.

reboot kept all 32 disabled, Home on the new launcher and its key services bound.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV / HDMI app: com.tcl.tv.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- The saved Wi-Fi network belonged to setupwraith (`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`). Forget the
network and join it again in Settings first; afterwards it belongs to android.uid.system and
setupwraith can be disabled without the TV dropping off Wi-Fi.
- The Vietnamese tab names on the stock Google TV home ("Màn hình chính", "Ứng dụng") and its TCL tab come
from com.tcl.partnercustomizer, not from the system locale (en-US here): with it disabled the stock home
shows "Home" and "Apps".
- Signing in to a Google account right after the list made Play Store install VTV Go, HBO Max and iQIYI
(installer com.android.vending). They are ordinary apps: uninstall them, and turn off auto-update in
Play Store settings.
- TclAppBoot leaves the launcher's key services unbound until `appops set com.gathin.tvhome
APP_AUTO_START allow` followed by `appops write-settings` (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md).
- Disabling dreamx: set screensaver_components to com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream first.
- Remote buttons with launcherx disabled, checked on the real remote: same codes as the C69B in
tcl-g10-google-tv/. With INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 and HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1, settings_key_keycodes 83 and
app_keys 4065:com.google.android.youtube.tv, 4062:com.netflix.ninja, Home, Input, Settings, YouTube,
Netflix and the mic (Assistant) all work.

mau.header:
TCL 65C735 (reports as "Smart TV Pro", device G05, product G05_4K_GB), Google TV 11 (SDK 30),
firmware AR2101, 2.7 GB RAM. France, wired through a USB Ethernet adapter (eth1).
Same platform as examples/tcl-g05-google-tv; this list is a little more conservative.

Also used on a TCL 55C728, Turkey (same product G05_4K_GB, build AR2101, software V8-T615T03-LF1V618,
security patch 2024-11-05, wired Ethernet), with these differences:
- com.tcl.ttvs stays enabled there, because the system updater lives in it (versionUpdateApp
SystemUpdateActivity): disabling it also stops OTA updates. Kept, it logs every remote key press for
TCL's BI (KeyDownBehaviorReceiver-BI) and turns com.tcl.usercenter and com.tcl.MultiScreenInteraction_TV
(T-Cast) back on at every boot, even after `pm uninstall --user 0`, so those two stay enabled as well.
- Eleven preloads came disabled from the factory on that unit (Abema, U-NEXT, Hulu JP, FOD, Stan,
Rakuten TV, both AirPlay packages, the game bar, notes, Alexa); com.tcl.assistant was left enabled.
- It also disabled the lines marked "55C728" below (commented out, so this list is unchanged).
Two days of use with several reboots; tools/check.py reported no drift. setupwraith stayed
disabled across reboots.
- config.json in this folder maps its remote: gear 4077 to Settings, Netflix 4062, YouTube 4065 and Prime
Video 4099 (install with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1). The TCL Channel button never reaches the accessibility
helpers, so it cannot be mapped. Firmware logs each press as `TclPhoneWindowManager:
handleKeyBeforeQueueing, key = <code>`; the main logcat buffer is 1 MiB, so read it right away.

Also used on a TCL 65C935, France (same product G05_4K_GB, build AR2101, incremental AR25, software
V8-T615T03-LF1V614, Wi-Fi only, MediaTek MT9615), with these notes:
- Applied in five batches with a screenshot between each; Home, the TCL Quick panel (Input key), HDMI,
Wi-Fi, Play Store and YouTube worked after every batch and after a reboot. One evening of use.
- com.tcl.ttvs kept (updater), as on the 55C728. It re-enables com.tcl.esticker within minutes and
com.tcl.usercenter, com.tcl.notereminder and com.tcl.smartalexa at every boot; tools/check.py reports
those four as drift. The 55C728 lines marked below were disabled on this unit too (logkit, channelplus,
useragreement, gtvpai, ocean.instructions, browser, miracast); Assistant and Chromecast kept.
- setupwraith owned TWO saved Wi-Fi networks: the one in use and an old SSID from a previous ISP.
Forgetting and re-joining the current one in Settings moved it to com.android.tv.settings, but
disable.sh still refused setupwraith because of the old one, which Settings offered no way to forget.
`cmd wifi list-networks` showed its id and `cmd wifi forget-network <id>` removed it. Disabling
setupwraith then survived a reboot (third AR2101 report; only tcl-g05-google-tv saw it come back).
- Remote: the same keycodes as the 55C728 (gear 4077, Netflix 4062, YouTube 4065, Prime Video 4099),
plus Input 178, which opens the TCL Quick panel with no helper. config.json applies unchanged;
settings_key_panel: true gives the gear the launcher's quick settings panel. Holding Volume+ still
auto-repeats with HomeKeyService bound (repeatCount climbed normally), so key_filter costs nothing here.
- After tools/theme.sh restarted Home, HomeKeyService was left enabled but UNBOUND (dumpsys
accessibility: "Bound services:{}") and the gear did nothing (#994). Clearing the list, toggling
accessibility_enabled off, waiting 2 s and writing it back bound it again; `appops set
com.gathin.tvhome AUTO_START allow; appops write-settings` first, and restore_key_services in the theme.
- `tools/tv.py 'reboot'` never returns on this set (#995): run it with a timeout.

Also used on a TCL 65C745 QLED, France (2023; same product G05_4K_GB, build AR2101, incremental AR25, software
V8-T615T03-LF1V614, security patch 2024-03-05, wired Ethernet, 32-bit armeabi-v7a), with these notes:
- Applied in seven batches with a screenshot between each. One day of use; several reboots, two of them checked
with tools/check.py (no drift). The 65C745 also comes as a G08 set on Google TV 14 (examples/tcl-55c745): read
ro.product.name before picking a list.
- Also disabled on this unit: the lines marked "65C745" below (commented out, so this list is unchanged), plus
Netflix, Prime Video, the stock YouTube app, Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell), T-Cast
(com.tcl.MultiScreenInteraction_TV) and the game bar, by choice. AirPlay kept by choice.
- com.tcl.ttvs disabled: TCL offers nothing past LF1V614 on this set. With it off, com.tcl.usercenter and T-Cast
stayed disabled across both reboots, where the 55C728 and 65C935 saw them come back.
- There is no separate Network/ADB debugging toggle: USB debugging alone opens port 5555.
- Two setup-time SSIDs were saved; with both forgotten and the set on Ethernet, disable.sh could read no network
owner and skipped setupwraith, so it went with FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1. Before that, build-and-install.sh rolled
Home back because setupwraith's RecoveryActivity claimed HOME, as described above.
- Remote (IR, "MStar Smart TV IR Receiver"): no Input 178 button. The source button, marked CH, sends KEY_EPG
(scancode 365), which Android does not map: "scan:365:inputs" in app_keys opens the Inputs menu once #1167 is in the launcher.
Gear 4077, Netflix 4062 and YouTube 4065 as on the 55C728.
- Volume: with a key-filtering helper bound (HomeKeyService or InputKeyService), each press of the remote's
volume key steps the volume twice; an injected KEYCODE_VOLUME_UP steps it once, and consuming the key in the
helper does not stop the double step. key_filter: false brings back one step per press, at the price of every
remote button mapped above.
- `appops set com.gathin.tvhome AUTO_START allow` fails here (Unknown operation string). After a theme push only
one of the two helpers was bound at a time; a reboot binds the enabled ones again.

mau.header:
TCL 65Q650G (US Q6 2023, reports as "Smart TV" / BeyondTV4), Android TV 11 (SDK 30), Realtek RTD2851
(client type TCL-NA-RTD51M), firmware V8-R51MT08-LF1V095, Google TV launcher

Same firmware family as examples/tcl-65q550g (a different model, tested over Ethernet there).

Tested 2026-10-20 on a real unit, applied in three batches with a screenshot after each: Home, the
remote's Input panel (com.tcl.suspension) and Live TV (com.tcl.tv/.TVActivity, all four HDMI ports in
TvInputManager) kept working. Quirks: Git Bash rewrites /data/... paths for tools/tv.py --pull, so set
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1; screencap to /sdcard fails here, use /data/local/tmp. Launcher installed with
tools/tv.py --push + pm install, later with build-and-install.sh (b64push md5 matched). Reboot-checked: all
packages stayed disabled, Home stayed on the new launcher, both key services re-bound.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (disabled by build-and-install.sh). setupwraith claims
HOME (priority 1) once it is off, so it is in group 1b. Check `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'` first:
on this unit the Wi-Fi network in use belonged to android.uid.system, so disabling setupwraith kept it.

Remote (Bluetooth BT_RC813_M1, /dev/input/event3, /system/usr/keylayout/Generic.kl):
- Input (TV_INPUT) and the mic keep working without launcherx.
- Netflix (242, TCL_NETFLIX), YouTube (245, TCL_YOUTUBE) and Prime Video (752, TCL_PRIMEVIDEO) do nothing
once launcherx is off: app_keys KEYCODE_TCL_NETFLIX:com.netflix.ninja, KEYCODE_TCL_YOUTUBE:
com.google.android.youtube.tv, KEYCODE_TCL_PRIMEVIDEO:com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom with
INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 bring them back (getevent -l names Prime KEY_PRIMEVIDEO; its scancode is 752, not 365).
- Gear (233, TCL_SET) also went dead; app_keys KEYCODE_TCL_SET did not catch it, settings_key_scancodes 233
with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 did.
- TclAppBoot refuses to start the key services at boot until `appops set com.gathin.tvhome APP_AUTO_START allow`.
All verified with the real remote, also after a reboot. Live TV app: com.tcl.tv (live_tv_package, hidden_apps).

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-ak30a5/debloat.txt com.tcl.cyberui
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.tcl.cyberui (a PERSISTENT priv-app — see the note below before disabling it).
Live TV / HDMI: com.tcl.tv. There is NO standard TvInputManager on this firmware (`service list`
has no tv_input), so the launcher's Inputs menu opens TCL's own source panel instead:
startService(com.tcl.settings/com.tcl.insrc.ShowWindowService, action com.tcl.insrc.SHOW_WINDOW).
Keep com.tcl.settings or that panel is gone. HDMI source ids: TV=2, AV1=3, HDMI1=8, HDMI2=9.
Keep com.tcl.tv: it owns DTV/HDMI playback and the remote's source key (KEYCODE_TV_INPUT still
opens the source panel over any launcher, cyberui or not).
Keep com.sohu.inputmethod.sogou.tv: it is the ONLY input method on the TV. Disable it and there is
no on-screen keyboard at all.
Keep com.tcl.guard: 电视卫士 is also the only on-screen APK installer (应用安装, needs a USB stick).
Keep com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter if you play anything from USB.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- `pm install` is patched to refuse shell installs ("install apk has be disabled from pm by
system default"), and PackageInstallerActivity is exported=false with its intent filters removed.
`pm install-commit` is not gated though: an APK can still be installed by creating a
PackageInstaller session from a shell-run app_process and committing that session.
- APKs that declare android.intent.category.HOME are refused at parse time unless they are signed
with TCL's key: "INSTALL_PARSE_FAILED_INCONSISTENT_CERTIFICATES: disable install launcher app not
signature by tcl". A third-party launcher therefore cannot be installed on this model at all;
com.tcl.cyberui stays and only its ad/telemetry packages (this list) can be removed.
- 电视卫士 → 应用安装, the only on-screen installer, stages the APK as a file without the .apk
suffix and fails with INSTALL_PARSE_FAILED_NOT_APK ("Failed to parse .../my_app_session") for
every package. Don't use it.
- Installs also need roughly 600 MB free on /data or they fail with
INSTALL_FAILED_INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE; `pm trim-caches 2000M` is usually enough.
- Installed launcher version here is com.tcl.cyberui 7746 (7.7.46). The 灵控桌面 APKs circulating
for TCL sets are the same package at versionCode 7670 (7.6.70), i.e. a downgrade.
- screensaver_components ships pointing at com.android.deskclock, which is not installed, so the
TV has no working screensaver out of the box (and launcher/'s Clock can't be installed here).
- /data/local/tmp is not writable by the shell user; push to /sdcard instead.
- `screencap` cannot write to /data/local/tmp either, and returns an empty file while Live TV/HDMI
is on screen (same as the G10). Press Home first.
- No com.android.dreams.basic fallback screensaver. Also no TCL equivalent of `pm install`.

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-g05-google-tv/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (pass it to restore.sh, the default is wrong here).
Live TV app: com.tcl.tv (.TVActivity; keep it, it also owns HDMI/antenna playback, HDMI through
com.tcl.tvinput's passthrough input). Keep com.tcl.tvinput, com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.system.server,
com.tcl.keyhelp, com.tcl.autopair, com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service (remote) and com.tcl.providers.config.
Unlike the G10, com.tcl.ttvs ships enabled here. It carries TCL's BI analytics and Samba TV ACR, and on AR71
also the TCL firmware updater (versionUpdateApp ... SystemUpdateActivity): comment it out to keep updates.
The firmware re-enables com.tcl.usercenter and com.tcl.smartalexa at every boot (55Q750G, two reboots);
everything else in the list stayed disabled.

Known quirk, read before replacing the launcher. Whether disabling setupwraith sticks goes by the
incremental build (ro.build.version.incremental), not by the model; all reports share the AR2101 build ID:
- AR68 (US, the unit this list came from): this US build is the exception. With launcherx disabled,
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity claims HOME at priority 1 and Home lands on a
black, looping recovery screen. Shell cannot disable that component. Disabling the whole setupwraith
package worked until a reboot, after which this TV had it back in charge, unlike the MOOR2, QM6K and
Chromecast reports where the disable survives. launcher/build-and-install.sh refuses and rolls back
while Home resolves to setupwraith (README, Troubleshooting).
Recover with: pm enable com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx; pm enable com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
- AR71 (US, a TCL 55Q750G, 21 October 2026): the first run of build-and-install.sh on G05 firmware.
setupwraith stayed disabled across a reboot and Home stayed with the new launcher (mFocusedApp =
com.gathin.tvhome). Order: setupwraith first, while launcherx still owns Home, then build-and-install.sh,
which starts the new launcher and only then disables launcherx. On Wi-Fi, run
`tools/tv.py "dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'"` first: the network saved during first setup belonged
to setupwraith, so disable.sh skips it. Forget the network and join it again in Settings, typing the
password, until `cmd wifi list-networks` shows a new network ID (the first forget there did not take); it
then belongs to com.android.tv.settings and Wi-Fi survives the disable. Input, Settings, Netflix, YouTube,
Prime Video and the mic all worked with launcherx off and com.tcl.suspension kept, without
INPUT_KEY_SERVICE or HOME_KEY_SERVICE.
- The G05_4K_GB units (tcl-65c735, and docs/devices/tcl-55c728-g05-4k-gb.md on AR28) kept setupwraith off
across a reboot too. The 55C728 report installed its own launcher, not with build-and-install.sh.
Compare ro.build.version.incremental before promising either outcome.
Contributed by damonearl (PR #73); AR71 findings from a 55Q750G.

Tested 2026-10-20 on a real unit, applied in six batches with screenshots between them: Wi-Fi, Home, the Input

setupwraith, launcherx and dreamx stayed disabled after a reboot (unlike the G05). Launcher works.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx; setupwraith's RecoveryActivity claims HOME at priority 1

Also tested 2026-10-19 on a second unit, UK firmware used in Brazil, build RP1A.200622.001 AR17, with the
launcher as Home and through a reboot. Two things differ from AR20 there:
- The Wi-Fi saved during first setup belonged to setupwraith, so disabling it made Android delete the
network and the TV dropped off Wi-Fi (and ADB). Pick the network again in Settings > Network; Settings
then owns it and it survives reboots. tools/disable.sh now checks the owner first and skips setupwraith
while it owns the network.
- The adb shell may not write Android/data, so tools/theme.sh has to go through the launcher's
ThemeProvider (it falls back to it on its own when the plain copy is refused).
TvInputManager reports AV as connected with nothing plugged in. com.tcl.notereminder was enabled on that
unit, not disabled at the factory, so it is listed below.

Also tested 2026-10-20/21 on a third unit in Brazil (product G07_4K_GB_NF, client TCL-LA-RTD51A-S1,
software V8-R51AT01-LF1V126, incremental AR07, fingerprint TCL/G07_4K_GB_NF/G07:11/RP1A.200622.001/AR17,
security patch 2024-12-05; Discussion #729):
- Stage 1 disabled 9 packages in two conservative batches (waterfall.overseas, esticker, notereminder,
feedback, guard, then dashboard, partnercustomizer, messagebox, tv.tclhome_passive) while keeping the
stock launcherx as Home. Stage 2 disabled 25 more packages, installed the reference launcher
(INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1) with the ClockDream screensaver, and disabled launcherx,
setupwraith (saved Wi-Fi belonged to android.uid.system, uid 1000) and dreamx.
- Kept by choice on that unit: com.tcl.ttvs (firmware updates), voice (com.google.android.katniss,
com.tcl.assistant, com.google.android.tv.assistant), Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell)
and com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic. Physical HDMI/AV playback, OTA update arrival and live
tools/restore.sh rollback were not exercised in that session.
- Only au.com.stan.and and tv.wuaki.apptv came disabled at the factory (com.tcl.smartalexa and
com.iqiyi.i18n.tv were not installed); com.google.android.videos and com.tcl.notereminder shipped
enabled.
- Reboot check (tools/check.py): launcherx, setupwraith, dreamx and the other disabled packages stayed
disabled across a reboot, but AR07 firmware automatically re-enabled com.tcl.notereminder and
com.tcl.usercenter at boot. Adding both to hidden_apps in launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml
hides them from the app grid without fighting the firmware on every boot.

Remote (IR, /dev/input/event0 "mtkinp"; scancodes from getevent with the real remote):
- Input (471, TV_INPUT) goes to TclPhoneWindowManager.startQuickPanelService, so it keeps working without
launcherx and needs no InputKeyService.
- Gear (561, TCL_SET) became launcherx's quick settings panel, so it does nothing once launcherx is off.
HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 with settings_key_scancodes 561 in config.xml brings it back.
- Netflix (566, TCL_NETFLIX) and YouTube (569, TCL_YOUTUBE) are broadcasts that only launcherx answers, so
they do nothing once it is off. An accessibility service that matches those scancodes and starts the app
fixes both (verified with the real remote).
Remote (Bluetooth, second AR20 unit, France; /dev/input/event3, vendor 0x0417 product 0x0304, Generic.kl):
- Its buttons send other codes, and settings_key_scancodes 561 does nothing for them. Gear is KEY_FORWARDMAIL
(233, TCL_SET) and arrives as keycode 4077; Prime Video is HID usage 0x000c005f and arrives as keycode 4099.
`getevent -lt` while pressing a button tells the two remotes apart (event0 mtkinp or event3).
- With HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1, this config.xml brought back Gear, Netflix, YouTube and Prime Video (verified with
the real remote): settings_key_keycodes 4077, and app_keys KEYCODE_TCL_NETFLIX:com.netflix.ninja,
KEYCODE_TCL_YOUTUBE:com.google.android.youtube.tv, 4099:com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom.
tools/b64push.py worked here (md5 match). Screenshots of Live TV and HDMI are 0 bytes; Netflix's are black.

com.tcl.autopair, com.google.android.tv.remote.service, com.tcl.inputmethod.international (the keyboard),
com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.system.server, com.tcl.providers.config, com.tcl.initsetup, com.tcl.factory.view,

Known quirks on this firmware:
- The red "TV" tile disappears from the Google TV Home row after this list (probably
com.tcl.partnercustomizer). TV stays in the Apps row and behind the Inputs tile.
- Disabling dreamx leaves screensaver_components pointing at it. Switch to the AOSP fallback with
tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.android.dreams.basic/.Colors'
On the 43P69K it also removes the screensaver menu from Settings. dreamx was re-enabled there;
leave its line commented out if you need that menu, even when using a third-party screensaver or the add-on photo-screensaver.
- screencap writes an empty file while Live TV/HDMI is on screen. Press Home first.
- The Google TV promo banner is drawn by launcherx itself, so only launcher/ removes it.
- Disabling the stock launcher alone is not enough to install a replacement:
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith (the setup wizard) also claims Home at a lower
priority and takes over once launcherx is disabled. Disable it too before setting the new
launcher as Home — launcher/build-and-install.sh does this automatically and rolls back if
Home doesn't land on the new launcher. List it in your own debloat file so restore.sh brings
it back. Confirmed on two separate 55P6K units.
- On the 43P69K, the saved setup Wi-Fi belonged to setupwraith (dumpsys wifi: cname=...setupwraith).
Forget and re-join it in Settings BEFORE disabling setupwraith, so the network belongs to Settings;
otherwise disabling its owner drops Wi-Fi and the ADB connection.
- TclAppBoot blocks the launcher's key services (and WireGuard's VPN) at every boot until the
package has APP_AUTO_START (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). Run `appops write-settings` after
`appops set com.gathin.tvhome APP_AUTO_START allow`: app-ops are saved lazily, and a plain
`reboot` drops the change. Confirmed on the C69B over three reboots.

============================================================================
ADB: read this before anything else. This build is much harder than the 2026 MT9653 sets.
============================================================================
There is no "Developer options" screen and no "Wireless debugging" row anywhere in the UI.
TCL replaced the whole Settings app: com.android.settings is NOT installed, the stock settings
package is com.tcl.setting and it only declares MainActivity, SceneActivity,
StartOtherAppActivity and SlicePermissionActivity. Searching every activity for "adb", "debug"
or "develop" through an activity launcher returns nothing, and
android.settings.APPLICATION_DEVELOPMENT_SETTINGS has no handler.

The only switch is 通用设置 -> 更多 -> ADB. It opens adbd in **TLS mode on a random high port**
(observed 40769, 35879, 41629, 46493 on the same unit, a new one on every toggle):
- the port answers an ADB CNXN with STLS and never speaks plaintext;
- `adb connect ip:port` fails, daemon trace shows
"Post-handshake SSL_peek failed [SSLV3_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_UNKNOWN]";
- mDNS advertises _adb-tls-connect._tcp (instance adb-<serial>-xxxx) but never
_adb-tls-pairing._tcp, so `adb pair` has nothing to talk to;
- 5555 is closed and no other listener speaks ADB (full 1-65535 scan: adbd, two TCL services,
DLNA on 16626, AirPlay on 38171).
Switching Wi-Fi shows the stock Android prompt "要允许通过此网络进行无线调试吗" (per-BSSID), which
proves the wireless-debugging framework is present but the pairing UI was removed.

The working path is USB:
1. dual male USB-A cable, PC side in a USB 3.0 port, TV side in a **USB 2.0** port;
2. ADB toggle ON, then `adb devices`: Windows enumerates USB\VID_18D1&PID_4EE7 with the serial
that matches the mDNS instance, and the TV shows "Allow USB debugging";
3. accept it (and "always allow"), then `adb tcpip 5555` and `adb connect <ip>:5555`.
The USB path only works while the ADB toggle stays on, and 5555 is lost on every reboot
(re-run `adb tcpip 5555` with the cable attached).

============================================================================
Sideloading and the launcher: both are locked, and the lock is not in the installer app.
============================================================================
Every APK is refused over adb, including apps that do not declare HOME:
adb install / pm install / cmd package install
-> INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE: Install not allowed for file:///data/app/vmdl*.tmp
Spoofing the installer package (-i com.tcl.guard, com.tcl.appmarket2, com.android.packageinstaller)
changes nothing. The rejection is logged by system_server (PackageManager), not only by the
com.android.packageinstaller verifier.

The only channel that installs normal APKs is a USB stick through 电视卫士 (com.tcl.guard).
Driving the system installer UI over adb gets further but still fails: file:// URIs are refused
outright on Android 14, and a MediaStore content:// URI
am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -t application/vnd.android.package-archive \
-d content://media/external/file/<id> --grant-read-uri-permission \
-n com.android.packageinstaller/.InstallStart
does show "应用未被认证，是否继续安装" and then fails with
verifier: signature not match for tcl com.gathin.tvhome, will not be installed !

Root cause, readable with:
content query --uri content://com.tcl.providers.config/all | grep InstallConfig
{"enable":"true","strategies":[
{"name":"safeStrategy","enable":"true","priority":"0"},
{"name":"blackListStrategy","enable":"true","packages":[],"priority":"1"},
{"name":"thridStrategy","enable":"false","packages":["com.dangbeimarket","com.shafa.market","com.ant.store.appstore"],"priority":"2"},
{"name":"launcherStrategy","enable":"true","packages":[],"priority":"3"},
{"name":"overDueStrategy","enable":"true","packages":[],"priority":"4"},
{"name":"pmStrategy","enable":"true","priority":"5"}]}
launcherStrategy is enabled with an empty allowlist, so a HOME package is only accepted if it is
signed with com.tcl.cyberui's key. The row cannot be edited from the shell: `content update`
returns 0 and silently ignores the write (verified by writing the Version row and reading it
back), the `content` CLI splits --bind on every ':' so a JSON value cannot be passed at all, and
/data/user_de/0/com.tcl.providers.config/databases/ is not readable as shell.

Stock launcher: com.tcl.cyberui, the only activity that resolves MAIN+HOME. Never disable it.
Net effect for this generation: debloat only. A replacement launcher is impossible without a
TCL-signed build, root, or a firmware downgrade.

Tested on a real unit: 28 packages disabled, one full `reboot` afterwards, Home, source panel,
Settings, app store, 电视卫士, Media Center and Multi-screen all still worked, crash buffer empty,
free RAM went from 1.97 GB to 1.15 GB (of 3.7 GB). Wait at least 10 seconds after applying before
rebooting.

Not present on this unit, so they are absent from the list: com.tcl.bi,
com.tcl.recognize.service, com.tcl.weixin, com.tcl.videocall.
Kept on purpose: com.tcl.cyberui, com.tcl.tv, com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.systemserver, com.tcl.ttvs,
com.tcl.providers.config, com.tcl.guard (USB install), com.tcl.appmarket2 (store),
com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter (USB playback), com.sohu.inputmethod.sogou.tv (only keyboard),
com.tcl.autopair (remote pairing), com.tcl.miracast, com.tcl.MultiScreenInteraction_TV,
com.tcl.systemui.plugin.* (source panel and quick settings), com.tcl.usercenter,
com.tcl.walleve (voice, left on by owner choice).

ADB, read this before anything else: there is no "Build number" tap seven times on this firmware
and no ADB row in developer options. Settings → About this device (关于本机) → Device info (本机信息),
then press UP DOWN LEFT RIGHT on the remote; the ADB toggle appears at the bottom. The sequence
often has to be repeated two or three times before it fires — a single pass looks like it did
nothing, so keep going instead of assuming the path is wrong. Once on, it stays on across
reboots:
persist.adb.tcp.port=5555, persist.service.adb.enable=1.

Stock launcher: com.tcl.cyberui — the only activity that resolves MAIN+HOME, so never disable it
(no HOME handler means a black screen on boot). A third-party launcher cannot be installed here:
the refusal is a package verification step, not a parse error (see tcl-ak30a5 for the older
Android 9 variant). Any APK declaring android.intent.category.HOME fails with
INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE and logs:
OverseasAppConfig: Verifying begin
verifier: fetch signature info from: com.tcl.cyberui
verifier: signature does not match for tcl <pkg>, will not be installed!
The gate is com.android.packageinstaller → verifier/InstallStrategyManager → LauncherStrategy,
which allows a HOME package only if it is in that strategy's package list, or is signed with
com.tcl.cyberui's key and carries <meta-data com.tcl.app.type="com.tcl.ui">. The list is TCL's
InstallConfig, readable with `content query --uri content://com.tcl.providers.config/all`
(project_id=InstallConfig) and not writable from the shell.

Sideloading is blocked for everything else too, not just launchers. On this unit `adb install`,
`pm install`, `pm install-commit` and launching the exported InstallStart activity by hand all
end in INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE — including an APK signed by TCL itself, and with
`-i com.tcl.appmarket2` spoofing the store as installer. Apps arrive through the TCL app store
(com.tcl.appmarket2) or a USB stick via 电视卫士. Don't spend an afternoon on adb install.

Live TV app: com.tcl.tv — keep it, it owns DTV/HDMI playback and the remote's source key.
Kept on purpose:
com.tcl.guard                 电视卫士; on this firmware the USB install path is the remaining
way to sideload, so keep it
com.tcl.appmarket2            TCL app store, the other install channel
com.sohu.inputmethod.sogou.tv the only input method; disable it and there is no keyboard at all
com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter        USB playback; the whole Media Center app goes with it
com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.systemserver, com.tcl.ttvs (holds DEVICE_ADMIN_ENABLED)

Applied on a real unit and re-checked after a full reboot (`reboot`, not standby): Home, the
source panel (HDMI 1-4 plus TV/AV/cast), Media Center, the app store, 电视卫士 and Settings all
still worked, with no entries in the crash buffer and no ANRs. Memory available went from 1.97 GB
to 2.24 GB. Voice and TCL account services are off by choice, noted per group below.

Expected in logcat afterwards, harmless: `Unable to start service ... com.tcl.usercenter` about
every 20 seconds. The bind fails immediately and starts no process.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- Play Protect blocks the launcher ("built for an older version of Android") unless targetSdk >= 34.
- With launcherx disabled, setupwraith's RecoveryActivity claims HOME at priority 1 and shows a blank
screen. Shell can't disable that one component, so the whole package is disabled below (it only
runs first-time setup). While Home was blank the TV fell back to HDMI 1 and woke a console over CEC.
- Gear (keycode 83) and YouTube (190) only reach launcherx, so both go dead once it is disabled.
config.json here maps them again; install the launcher with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 so the accessibility
service binds and reads them, then push the theme:
TV_HOST=<tv ip> HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 launcher/build-and-install.sh
TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/theme.sh examples/tcl-qm6k-google-tv
- Soundbar on optical (S/PDIF) can't be powered or volume-controlled by the TV. Use HDMI 4 (eARC) and
`cmd hdmi_control cec_setting set system_audio_control 1` (it ships 0 here).

Live TV app:    com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter (.nav.TurnkeyUiMainActivity) — NEVER disable it.
NOT the live TV app: com.cltv.fast ("FAST" streaming channels, iWedia). Its activities ship
